pr_title: C#: Make internal properties and property accessors public (but hidden)
pr_body:
Instead of making the accessors `internal` which can break binary compat, make them `public` but hide them with EB never so they don't show up in IntelliSense.

Also, do the same for properties with the `PROPERTY_USAGE_INTERNAL` flag. These properties were not meant to be exposed to scripting, but since they've been public before all we can do now is hide them.

- I _think_ this closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/71062 since the property that was confusing should now be hidden.
pr_comments:
I like this generally, but one potential compatibility issue:
Does it count as shadowing/blocking `internal` methods of parent classes in C#?

I.e. if I extend `Animation` and I decided to add a `GetLength` method to it, will this break now that `Animation.GetLength` goes from `internal` to `public`? Regardless of that being appropriate or not it's not a method anyone would know existed

Edit: To be clear I don't think it's a major issue, and we often add new methods and that might trigger the same effect, but we're exposing methods en-masse here and it's worth thinking about I think, especially since they're hidden they might cause confusion, depending on how it's handled in C# (I don't know enough of C#, it's been years since I worked with it, so it might just be fine to have shadowing etc.)

> I.e. if I extend `Animation` and I decided to add a `GetLength` method to it, will this break now that `Animation.GetLength` goes from `internal` to `public`?

It doesn't break binary compatibility if that's what you are asking. Your `GetLength` method shadows the inherited method and that will now give you a [warning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/compiler-messages/cs0108) that you can suppress with the [`new` modifier](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/keywords/new-modifier) if shadowing was intended.
That answers my question that the warning isn't an issue as such, as opposed to virtual methods in C++ etc., good!

issue_context.title: [C# API] Possible type mismatch of property Node.AnchorsPreset
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0 beta 10

### System information

Irrevalent

### Issue description

The property Node.AnchorsPreset should be of type LayoutPreset just like what Node.SetAnchorsPreset takes, but it is now of type int. This is difficult for users to figure out which preset each int value stands for, which makes the property unusable. Its type should be changed to LayoutPreset instead. 

### Steps to reproduce

N/A

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
The C# API is generated from ClassDB, this property is defined in Core as taking an INT which is why C# also defines it that way:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/fcba87e696d58912838d8a4a6987b10efa28e78f/scene/gui/control.h#L285-L286

Additionally, setting the Node.AnchorsPreset property may result in unexpected results, while the SetAnchorsPreset function always gives the correct result. Maybe make Node.AnchorsPreset a readonly property and guide users to the SetAnchorsPreset function for modifying?

The `Control.AnchorsPreset` property uses the `_SetAnchorsLayoutPreset` method internally, it's not the same as calling `SetAnchorsPreset`, they're two different APIs. Someone from the @godotengine/gui-nodes team can explain better how these APIs work but basically `_SetAnchorsLayoutPreset` sets the anchors preset (like `SetAnchorsPreset`) but also sets the offset preset and the grow direction preset, maybe renaming the property to `anchors_layout_preset` would make the difference clearer.

> The `Control.AnchorsPreset` property uses the `_SetAnchorsLayoutPreset` method internally, it's not the same as calling `SetAnchorsPreset`, they're two different APIs. Someone from the @godotengine/gui-nodes team can explain better how these APIs work but basically `_SetAnchorsLayoutPreset` sets the anchors preset (like `SetAnchorsPreset`) but also sets the offset preset and the grow direction preset, maybe renaming the property to `anchors_layout_preset` would make the difference clearer.

Thanks for your explanation!

Both `anchors_preset` and `layout_mode` are not supposed to be used in scripting. They are marked as `PROPERTY_USAGE_INTERNAL`, and are only relevant for the editor. They exist as properties because that's the only way to have them in the inspector and in a specific order.

Now, GDScript doesn't hide those properties either, because `PROPERTY_USAGE_INTERNAL` is for the most part only used for documentation. So it's not an issue with the C# generator, but it's probably something we should address across the board. I don't think renaming either would be a good option here: the name is clear in each context and you are not supposed to interact with both of them in the same context.

The collision is accidental, and the property and the method have no relation. The `set_anchors_preset` method is just a helper method to set all anchors together according to a `LayoutPreset` value. The `anchors_preset` property accepts different values than `LayoutPreset` (we just happen to reuse that enum internally for validation to reduce duplication of such a large enumeration). They are not compatible for each other.

Hi! Interested in working on this issue. After reading the discussion, I'm unsure of what needs to be done here. It sounds as though things are behaving as intended? Or does there need to be a type change in ClassDB to fix the C# type?
Hey, sorry, there is no consensus yet on what should be done here. And this shouldn't be marked as a good first issue, at least not until we reach one.
